body:
PR #1989 BUILD IS GREEN at 20881480b8, MERGEABLE. But only ONE of your two hold
clauses is stale, and I want to flag something my fix did to the other.

YOUR HOLD SAYS:
  (a) "build red"  -- now stale. Build (ubuntu-latest) passes, 10m39s.
  (b) "the split classifies NeedsAttention -> InProgress as disposition, which
      blocks the reviewer-finding-to-rework cycle this spec was written to
      unblock. Rework directed on the spec."

(b) IS UNTOUCHED BY ANYTHING I DID. I fixed two mechanical CI failures -- a
discipline-pack sync and a test asserting the pre-change behaviour. I did not
address your design objection and I am not claiming to have.

AND HERE IS THE PART YOU SHOULD KNOW BEFORE DECIDING: MY FIX PINS THE BEHAVIOUR
YOU ARE OBJECTING TO. The test now asserts, as a binding criterion, that without
advisor authority the transition is REFUSED and the spec stays parked. If you
rule that the gate is wrong, that test has to change with it -- it is no longer
just a stale assertion, it is a test that encodes the contested semantics. I
made your objection slightly more expensive to act on and you should have that
cost visible rather than discovering it in the rework.

If I had read your hold text before fixing rather than after, I would have asked
you first. I read "build red" and treated the whole hold as a CI problem.

ONE FACT THAT MAY BEAR ON (b), offered as input not as an argument. has_advisor_
authority() grants authority to an ORCHESTRATED drain -- the BUG-460 comment at
lib.rs:44179 says so explicitly, so --no-human drains can auto-queue review and
let phase children mutate. So the gate does not block the drain's own rework
cycle; it blocks a bare headless agent and a non-advisor seat. Whether that is
the cycle you meant, I do not know -- you wrote the hold and I would rather ask
than assume. If you meant the drain path, the gate may already be narrower than
the objection assumes. If you meant a hand-dispatched or product-seat rework,
the objection stands exactly as written, and tonight is evidence for it: I was
refused on that transition twice.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: clearing the hold, or asking you to. It is yours, clause (b)
is a live design call, and the independence rule keeps me out of it -- I have a
commit on this branch now.

STATE OF THE FOUR I TOUCHED TONIGHT:
  #2045 STORY-1391  MERGED
  #2029 BUG-1476    MERGED
  #2035 BUG-1470    green, REFUSED by reviewer on F1, held -- correctly
  #1989 STORY-1353  green, held on your clause (b)
subject: PR #1989 green — but only your 'build red' clause is stale, and my test now PINS the semantics you objected to
